mainTopic: Buying three trees: how much land comes with them, the allowed spacing of four to sixteen cubits, and follow-up questions on measuring and on which trees count
overview: This amud asks how much land a buyer gets when he buys trees, and how far apart the trees must be. רב יוסף finishes a story: רב יהודה ruled that a tree buyer gets land 'enough for an ox and its equipment,' and רב יוסף later worked out from a משנה and a ברייתא that this means four cubits. The גמרא explains that a real ruling (מעשה) is stronger proof than a משנה taught only in study. It then shows where each view gets its closest and farthest distances between the trees. רב יוסף follows רבי שמעון, with four to eight cubits. רב נחמן follows רבנן, with eight to sixteen cubits, and the closest distance is worked out by logic as half the farthest. רבא rules that anywhere from four to sixteen cubits counts, and a ברייתא agrees: with correct spacing and one purchase, the buyer owns the land and keeps it even if a tree dies. רבי ירמיה asks where on the tree we measure, and whether three branches of one buried tree count as three trees. רב גביהה answers both from vine laws in כלאים. רב פפא's question about a tree on the border or in a neighbor's field ends in תיקו.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ruling in the shepherds' village
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells how a tree-sale case came before רב יהודה. רב יהודה ruled that the buyer gets land 'enough for an ox and its equipment,' but רב יוסף did not know how much that was.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in a village of shepherds. They came before רב יהודה, and he told the seller: 'Go and give the buyer land as much as an ox and its equipment need.' But I did not know how much 'enough for an ox and its equipment' is.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is finishing a story about a real case where רב יהודה ruled on how much land comes with trees that were sold. He admits he did not understand the measure רב יהודה used, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer of trees gets some land around them so he can take care of them. רב יהודה gave the size of that land as 'כמלא בקר וכליו,' the space an ox and its plow need to work. רב יהודה did not give a number, so the measure is still unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: As much space as an ox and its equipment need

phrases.english: in a village of shepherds,
and they came before Rav Yehuda,
and he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the seller of the trees.

phrases.english: 'Go, give him'
as much as an ox and its equipment need';
and I did not know
phrases.notes: The 'I' here is רב יוסף, who is telling the story.

phrases.english: how much 'enough for an ox and its equipment' is;

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל הַב לֵיהּ כִּמְלֹא בָּקָר וְכֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's story from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer of the trees gets land 'enough for an ox and its equipment' to work them.

steps.title: Working out the measure as four cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף learns a משנה requiring four cubits between a tree and a neighbor's field, and a ברייתא that says this is for vineyard work. He concludes that 'enough for an ox and its equipment' means four cubits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I heard what we learned in a משנה: 'A person may not plant a tree close to his fellow's field unless he keeps it four cubits away,' and a ברייתא taught about it: 'The four cubits they said are for the work of the vineyard,' I said: learn from this that 'enough for an ox and its equipment' is four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains how he figured out the unclear measure. He uses a משנה and a ברייתא that explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a number, four cubits, and the ברייתא explains its purpose: room to work the trees. Working the trees is done with an ox and its plow, so it is the same idea as רב יהודה's measure. That links רב יהודה's measure to a fixed number: four cubits.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא taught about it

steps.whatToRemember: 'כמלא בקר וכליו' = four cubits, the room needed to work a tree with an ox and plow.

phrases.english: once I heard that which we learned in a Mishnah:
A person may not plant a tree
close to his fellow's field,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִרְחִיק מִמֶּנָּה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת;
phrases.english: unless he kept it four cubits away from it;
and it was taught about it:
The four cubits that they said —
are for the work of the vineyard;
I said: learn from it,
'enough for an ox and its equipment' is four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the uncertainty raised at the end of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כמלא בקר וכליו' equals four cubits.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about keeping a tree four cubits from a neighbor's field, and the ברייתא explaining it is for vineyard work.

steps.title: Why not cite the משנה in כלאים that fits רב יוסף?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: there is a משנה in כלאים that supports רב יוסף, so why bring a story instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn a משנה that fits רב יוסף? רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון say: One who plants his vineyard with eight cubits between rows on each side may bring seed there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף's view is backed by a story when a משנה already seems to back it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when vines are eight cubits apart, you may plant seeds between them. That means the vines are not treated as one connected vineyard. This fits רב יוסף's view about trees spread eight cubits apart, so the גמרא asks why this clear written source was not used.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn? (pointing to a source that should have been cited)

phrases.english: And didn't we learn a Mishnah in line with Rav Yosef?!
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon say:
One who plants his vineyard
eight cubits by eight,
phrases.notes: There are eight cubits of open space between the rows of vines in each direction.

phrases.english: is permitted to bring seed there!
phrases.notes: Normally planting grain near vines is forbidden as כלאים; here the vines are far enough apart that it is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רב יוסף's view was proven: why use a story when a משנה exists?
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to support רב יוסף with a story rather than a משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that says vines eight cubits apart are not one unit already supports רב יוסף, so citing a story seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A real-life ruling is better proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even so, a practical ruling (מעשה) is stronger proof than a teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, a real case is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. A real ruling counts for more than a teaching alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that the משנה supports רב יוסף. It explains that a real-life ruling shows the חכמים actually decided cases this way, which is stronger than a teaching that may only be in theory.

keyTerms.meaning: A practical case is better (stronger proof)

steps.whatToRemember: מעשה רב: a ruling that was actually carried out is stronger proof than a ruling taught only in theory.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule in the גמרא: a real ruling counts as stronger proof than a ruling only taught in study.

phrases.english: Even so, a real case is better.
phrases.notes: He means the real ruling that was brought earlier to back רב יוסף.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the choice of source: a real ruling is preferred over a teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a משנה supports רב יוסף, it should have been the source cited.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה does support him, but a real-life ruling is stronger proof, so the story is cited.

steps.title: For רב יוסף, both the closest and farthest distances have sources
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב יוסף, following רבי שמעון, has a source for both the farthest distance and the closest distance between the trees. The closest distance, four cubits, comes from a משנה in כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out fine for רב יוסף, who follows רבי שמעון: we know his farthest distance and we know his closest distance. The farthest is what we already said. The closest comes from a משנה: a vineyard planted with less than four cubits between the rows is not a vineyard, says רבי שמעון. The חכמים say it is a vineyard, and we look at the middle rows as if they are not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יוסף's view has a source for both numbers. This is a setup: next the גמרא will ask whether רב נחמן's view has the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every opinion needs two limits: how far apart the trees may be, and how close together. For רבי שמעון, the farthest limit was already stated, and the closest limit is four cubits, because he says rows closer than four cubits do not make a vineyard. So רב יוסף has a clear source for both.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine for… (the first half of a 'this side is fine, but that side is a problem' question)
According to, following the opinion of

steps.confusionAlert: Two different disagreements are mixed together here. רב יוסף and רב נחמן disagree about which תנא to follow. רבי שמעון and the חכמים disagree about vineyard spacing. רב יוסף follows רבי שמעון, and רב נחמן follows רבנן (the חכמים).

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן –
phrases.english: It works out fine for רב יוסף, who follows רבי שמעון:
we have heard his view on trees spread apart,
and we have heard his view on trees close together.
Spread apart: what we already said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה in step 3: רבי שמעון lets you plant seed between vines that are eight cubits apart.

phrases.english: Close together: as we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: כֶּרֶם הַנָּטוּעַ עַל פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת –
phrases.english: A vineyard planted with less than four cubits between the rows
is not a vineyard. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
And the חכמים say: it is a vineyard,
and we view the middle rows as if they are not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion comparing the sources behind רב יוסף's and רב נחמן's distance rules.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's (רבי שמעון's) minimum distance of four cubits
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה כלאים: a vineyard with rows less than four cubits apart is not a vineyard, according to רבי שמעון

steps.title: For רב נחמן, where does the closest distance come from?
steps.stepSummary: For רב נחמן, following רבנן, we know the farthest distance, but no source gives the closest distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב נחמן, who follows רבנן, we have heard the farthest distance. Have we heard the closest distance?!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא raises the problem: רב נחמן's view seems to be missing a source for how close the trees may be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The farthest distance for רבנן (sixteen cubits) is known. No source gives the closest distance according to רבנן. So רב נחמן's view seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: But (the second, problem half of a בשלמא question)
Have we heard this from him? (Meaning: we have not.)

phrases.english: But for רב נחמן, who follows רבנן:
we have heard their view on trees spread apart,
but have we heard their view on trees close together?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא question: רב יוסף is fine, but רב נחמן seems to lack a source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No source gives רבנן's minimum distance between the trees.

steps.title: Logic: the closest distance is half the farthest
steps.stepSummary: The closest distance comes from logic. For רבי שמעון it is half the farthest distance, so for רבנן it is also half: eight cubits.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is based on logic. Since for רבי שמעון the closest distance is half the farthest, for רבנן it is also half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not need a source here, because logic fills in the missing number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the closest limit (four) is half the farthest limit (eight). We apply the same ratio to רבנן: half of sixteen is eight. So רב נחמן's range is eight to sixteen cubits.

phrases.english: It is based on logic:
since for רבי שמעון it is half,
phrases.notes: Four cubits is half of eight.

phrases.english: for רבנן it is also half.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical derivation from a parallel ratio
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a direct source, רב נחמן seemed to have no minimum distance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The minimum is half the maximum, so eight cubits according to רבנן.

steps.title: רבא's ruling: from four to sixteen cubits
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the trees count if they are anywhere from four to sixteen cubits apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה is from four cubits up to sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final practical ruling on the allowed spacing between the trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא takes the smallest number (four, from רבי שמעון) and the largest number (sixteen, from רבנן). This gives the widest possible range, which favors the buyer.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: three trees between four and sixteen cubits apart give the buyer the land.

phrases.english: רבא said: the הלכה is
from four cubits up to sixteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views are explained, רבא gives the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The allowed spacing is anywhere from four to sixteen cubits.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the trees may be as close as four cubits and as far as sixteen, just like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבא: How close may they be? Four cubits. How far apart may they be? Sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the same two limits, four and sixteen. So רבא's ruling is not only his own combination of the two views; an earlier source says the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבא:
How close may they be? Four cubits.
And how far apart may they be? Sixteen.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's range of four to sixteen cubits
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving four cubits as the minimum and sixteen as the maximum

steps.title: What the buyer gets, and when he gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: with correct spacing, the buyer gets the land and the trees between, and keeps the land even if a tree dies. With wrong spacing, or if he bought the trees one at a time, he gets neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has bought the land and the trees between them. So if a tree dries up or is cut down, he still has the land. If the spacing is less than this or more than this, or he bought them one after the other, he has bought neither the land nor the trees between them. So if a tree dries up or is cut down, he has no land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining what the buyer actually owns in each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the spacing is right, the land itself becomes the buyer's, so it stays his even after a tree is gone. When the spacing is wrong, or the trees were bought one at a time and not all three together, he owns only the trees themselves. Then, once a tree is gone, he has no land.

keyTerms.meaning: One after the other (not all in one purchase)

steps.whatToRemember: Three trees bought together, spaced four to sixteen cubits apart, give the buyer the land and the trees in between. Otherwise he gets only the trees.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us whether the buyer keeps any land after his trees are gone, which is the practical heart of the whole discussion.

phrases.english: he has bought the land
and the trees that are between them.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, יָבֵשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ נִקְצַץ – יֵשׁ לוֹ קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: Therefore, if a tree dried up or was cut down, he still has the land.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כָּאן,
phrases.english: If the spacing is less than this or more than this,
or if he bought them one after the other,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא קָנָה לֹא אֶת הַקַּרְקַע
phrases.english: he has bought neither the land
nor the trees that are between them.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, יָבֵשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ נִקְצַץ – אֵין לוֹ קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: Therefore, if a tree dried up or was cut down, he has no land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה קָנָה קַרְקַע וְאֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 9 and gives the legal results of the spacing rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With correct spacing and one purchase, the buyer gets the land and the trees between. Otherwise he gets no land.

steps.title: Where on the tree do we start measuring?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the four-to-sixteen אמות distance is measured from the narrow part of the tree or the wide part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: When someone measures the distance between the trees, does he measure from the narrow place or from the wide place?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a practical follow-up to רבא's rule: from which point on the tree do we measure the gap?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree is thin in some places and wide in others, like a narrow trunk versus a spreading base. The answer could decide whether trees that are borderline in distance fall inside or outside the four-to-sixteen range.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (a real open question, not an attack)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
When he measures,
phrases.notes: He means measuring the four-to-sixteen אמות between the trees from Step 8.

phrases.english: does he measure from the narrow place,
or does he measure from the wide place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the measurement rule just established by רבא and the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the distance between trees is measured from the narrow or the wide part of the tree.

steps.title: Proof from measuring a bent-down vine
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה brings a משנה: for a vine branch bent into the ground, we measure only from the second root.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה of בי כתיל said to רב אשי: Come and hear, as we learned in a משנה: For a vine's bent-down branch, one measures only from the second root.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גביהה answers רבי ירמיה's question by quoting a משנה from מסכת כלאים about measuring a vine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה we do not measure from the widest spread of the vine. We measure from one set point, the second root. By comparison, here too we would not measure from the widest part of the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
As we learned in a משנה
A vine branch bent down into the ground that comes back up
The second root, where the bent branch rises again

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Geviha of Bei Khatil said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as we learned in a mishnah:
The bent-down branch of the vine —
he measures only from the second root.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 from a parallel משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Just as the vine is measured from the second root and not its widest spread, the trees are not measured from their widest part.

steps.title: Do three branches of one tree count as three trees?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about selling three branches that grow from one tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If he sold him three branches of a tree, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a second question: if the three 'trees' are really branches of one tree, do they count as three trees for the buyer to get the land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is when the trunk is covered with earth, so the branches stick up and look like three separate trees. The question is whether looks are enough, or whether we need three real trees.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If he sold him three branches of a tree,
phrases.notes: Picture the trunk buried in earth, so the three branches come up looking like three separate trees.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מָכַר לוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה בַּדֵּי אִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about what counts as 'three trees' in the sale.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether three branches of one buried tree count as three trees so that the buyer gets the land.

steps.title: Proof from three layered vines
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה quotes a משנה: three layered vines whose roots show combine if they are four to eight אמות apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה of בי כתיל said to רב אשי: Come and hear, as we learned in a משנה: One who bends three vines into the ground, and their roots can be seen, רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק says: If there are four to eight אמות between them, they combine; if not, they do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גביהה answers the branch question with another משנה from כלאים about vines bent into the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the parts that come up out of the ground are treated as separate plants that join together, as long as the spacing is right. So here too, branches of one buried tree count as separate trees if they are spaced correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: One who bends a vine branch into the ground so it takes root
They join together and count as one group

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבי ירמיה's questions are answered from vine laws in כלאים: we don't measure from the widest part, and branches that look like separate trees count as separate if spaced correctly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Geviha of Bei Khatil said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as we learned in a mishnah:
One who bends three vines into the ground,
and their roots can be seen —
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶן מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד שְׁמוֹנֶה –
phrases.english: If there are between them from four cubits up to eight —
they combine,
and if not — they do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע, דִּתְנַן: הַמַּבְרִיךְ שָׁלֹשׁ גְּפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 from a parallel משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Parts of one plant that come up separately count as separate plants when properly spaced, so the three branches count as three trees.

steps.title: Trees on the border or in two different fields
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether three trees still count together if one is on the border, or if one is in another person's field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If he sold him two trees inside his field and one on the border, what is the law? Two in his own field and one in his fellow's field, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks two more cases where the three trees are not all inside one field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally three trees in one field earn the buyer the land between them. Here one tree is on the edge, or in someone else's field. The question is whether the three still join together as one group.

keyTerms.meaning: The border or edge of a field

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he sold him two trees inside his field
and one on the border, what is the law?
Two inside his own field
and one inside his fellow's field, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another follow-up question about which three trees count together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether three trees combine when one stands on the border or in another person's field.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's question is left standing with no answer: תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying רב פפא's question has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי ירמיה's two questions, which were answered from משניות, no source settles רב פפא's cases. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no.' It means we don't know the answer either way.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 15's question without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether trees on the border or in another's field combine with the others remains undecided.
